{{nihongo|'''Hoshinomiya-sha Shrine'''|星宮社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

=== Overview ===
It is an old shrine that is said to have been founded in the {{ill|Asuka period|Q210688|qid=Q210688}}, and the name ``Hoshizaki'' appears in an old poem from the end of the Heian period, so it seems The plaque on the shrine building says ``Hoshizaki Shrine'', the ``{{ill|Owari meisho zue|ff|Owari meisho zue|ja|尾張名所図会|qid=Q11465290}}'' written in the late Edo period says ``Hoshi no Miya'', and the ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Owari Makiyuki}}'' says ``Hoshimiya Daimyojin''.After the {{ill|Edo period|lt=Edo period|qid=Q184963}}, many {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiogama}} were dotted around the area, so Hoshimiya Shrine was named in {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}{{ill|Aichi District|Q552687|qid=Q552687|lt=Aichi District}} A theory spread that it was ``Kamichigama Shrine'' or ``Shimochigama Shrine'' {{Sfn|Nagoya Local Culture Association|1980|pp=7-13}}. However, in recent years, Aichi-gun {{ill|Aichi District|Q552687|qid=Q552687|lt=Chigama-go}} from the south of the current {{ill|Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|ar|ناكامورا-كو|cs|Nakamura-ku (Nagoja)|es|Nakamura-ku (Nagoya)|eu|Nakamura-ku (Nagoia)|fa|ناکامورا-کو، ناگویا|fr|Nakamura-ku|id|Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|it|Nakamura-ku|ja|中村区|ko|나카무라구|pl|Nakamura (Nagoja)|th|เขตนากามูระ|tl|Nakamura-ku, Nagoya|tr|Nakamura|uk|Район Накамура|ur|ناکامورا وارڈ، ناگویا|vi|Nakamura, Nagoya|zh|中村区|qid=Q780521}} to the north of {{ill|Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|ar|ناكاغاوا-كو|arz|ناكاجاوا-كو، ناجويا|ceb|Nakagawa-ku|es|Nakagawa-ku (Nagoya)|fa|ناکاگاوا-کو، ناگویا|fr|Nakagawa-ku|id|Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|it|Nakagawa-ku|ja|中川区|ko|나카가와구|pl|Nakagawa (Nagoja)|th|เขตนากางาวะ|tl|Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|tr|Nakagawa, Nagoya|uk|Район Накаґава|ur|ناکاگاوا وارڈ، ناگویا|vi|Nakagawa, Nagoya|zh|中川區|qid=Q1155226}} The theory that it is compared to Nagoya Prefecture is now considered to be the most likely, and the theory that our company is Shigechigama Shrine has been denied {{Sfn|Nagoya Folk Culture Association|1980|pp=7-13}}. Shimochigama Shrine, which is a separate shrine within the precincts, is not mentioned in the ``{{ill|Kanbunmuramuraoboegaki|Q137766629|qid=Q137766629}}'' established in the early Edo period, and it is presumed that it was enshrined after the mid-Edo period {{Sfn|Nagoya Folk Culture Association|1980|pp=7-13}}.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
{{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} According to the Owari Makiyukiki written in 1822, it was founded ``at the time of Emperor Jomei's visit to Yushinden.'' The entry for Hoshizakisho (Minamino Village) mentions the ``Minamino Meteorite,'' and says that it may have come to be called ``Hoshi-sha (Hoshimiya-sha)'' because this meteorite fell. It is thought that it may have been founded by the Yamaguchi clan, a descendant of the Ouchi clan, who valued the faith of K|Myoken Bodhisattva|Q10960623}}. However, since the Minamino meteorite, which is the material for consideration, fell in the early Edo period, the chronology is reversed and contradictory. Owari Makiyuki also notes that this shrine may have been enshrined in the early modern period for another reason: ``The name book of the Aichi gods shows that samurai children visited this shrine.''

{{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} The Owarishi of 1844 cites an editorial that states that in the 9th year of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ar|الإمبراطور جوميه|azb|جومی (ایمپیراتور)|cs|Džomei|de|Jomei|es|Jomei Tennō|fa|امپراتور جومی|fr|Jomei|he|ג'ומנה|id|Kaisar Jomei|it|Jomei|ja|舒明天皇|ka|ძიომეი|ko|조메이 천황|mr|जोमेइ|nl|Jomei|pl|Jomei|pt|Jomei|ru|Император Дзёмэй|sh|Car Jomei|simple|Emperor Jomei|sl|Cesar Džomei|sv|Jomei|th|จักรพรรดิโจเม|tl|Emperador Jomei|tr|Jomei (imparator)|uk|Імператор Дзьомей|uz|Imperator Jomei|vi|Thiên hoàng Jomei|yo|Emperor Jomei|zh|舒明天皇|zh_min_nan|Zyomei Thian-hông|zh_yue|舒明天皇|qid=Q329761}} ({{ill|637|ab|637|af|637|am|637 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|637|ar|637|ary|637|ast|637|avk|637|az|637|azb|۶۳۷ (میلادی)|bar|637|be|637|be_x_old|637|bg|637|bn|৬৩৭|bpy|মারি ৬৩৭|br|637|bs|637.|ca|637|cdo|637 nièng|ce|637 шо|ceb|637|ckb|٦٣٧|crh|637|cs|637|cv|637|cy|637|da|637|de|637|el|637|eml|637|eo|637|es|637|et|637|eu|637|fa|۶۳۷ (میلادی)|fi|637|fo|637|fr|637|fy|637|ga|637|gan|637年|gd|637|gl|637|he|637|hi|637|ht|637 (almanak jilyen)|hu|637|hy|637|id|637|io|637|it|637|ja|637年|jv|637|ka|637|kk|637 жыл|ko|637년|la|637|lb|637|lij|637|lmo|637|lt|637 m.|map_bms|637|mdf|637|mg|637|mhr|637|mk|637|mr|इ.स. ६३७|mrj|637 и|ms|637|mzn|۶۳۷|nah|637|nap|637|nds|637|new|सन् ६३७|nl|637|nn|637|no|637|nso|637|oc|637|or|୬୩୭|os|637-æм аз|pl|637|pnb|637|pt|637|qu|637|ro|637|ru|637 год|rue|637|sa|६३७|scn|637|sd|637ع|se|637|sh|637.|shn|637|si|637|sk|637|sl|637|sq|637|sr|637|su|637|sv|637|sw|637|tg|Соли 637|th|พ.ศ. 1180|tk|637|tl|637|tly|637|tr|637|tt|637 ел|uk|637|ur|637ء|uz|637|vec|637|vi|637|war|637|wuu|637年|xmf|637|zh|637年|zh_min_nan|637 nî|zh_yue|637年|qid=Q33294}}), seven stars descended from the sky and there was an oracle, so a shrine was built in this area, which was the old Chiba village. The book suggests that the landowner deity that had been enshrined in this area since ancient times was not Seimiya Shrine, but Jochichigama Shrine, and that this shrine transformed into Myoken worship in the 9th year of Emperor Jomei's reign.

{{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 2nd year (1913) Aichi County Magazine states that in September 9th year of Emperor Jomei, {{ill|Oracle|Q217123|qid=Q217123}} ``built the first star shrine in Chiga no Sato.''The name of Hoshimiya Shrine is not listed in the domestic Shinto name book of Owari Province.

At the time of its founding, Hoshimiya Shrine was built near what is now Kasadera Elementary School (Hoshizaki Castle Ruins), but there is a theory that it was moved to its current location when {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} built {{ill|Hoshizaki Castle|Q2969408|qid=Q2969408}}. The current site of the shrine was at the edge of Hoshizaki Cape on the Kasadera Plateau <ref name="Minami-ku" />.

In ancient times, the Kasadera Plateau was known as Matsuko Island (Matsuko Island, Matsuko Island). It is said that there was a mansion of {{ill|Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11465294|qid=Q11465294}}'s {{ill|Otoyo no mikoto|Q97706258|qid=Q97706258}} (the enshrined deity of Kamichi Gama Shrine) in a place called ``Kunizo Owari|Q11465294}}.

[[Image:Yobitsugi-jinja Shrine Haiden, Hoshizaki Minami Ward Nagoya 2022.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Kanjosha, which enshrines the Minamino meteorite. <br />(Hoshizaki, Minami Ward, Nagoya City, January 2022)]]
Records and legends about stars and meteorites have existed in the Hoshizaki area since ancient times. There are the following theories regarding the place name Hoshizaki.

* Owari Makiyuki is written by {{ill|Jōhei|Q1324874|qid=Q1324874|lt=Johei}}5 years (935), when the {{ill|Tengyō no Ran|Q2975322|qid=Q2975322|lt=Taira no Masakado Rebellion}} occurred, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Imperial Order}} records the tradition that he prayed for {{ill|Shofuku|Q24897750|qid=Q24897750}} at Atsuta Daimyojin (Atsuta Shrine). Another story states that in the ``Atsuta annual event,'' the mikoshi from Atsuta Shrine was handed over to Seimiya Shrine. When the shrine family prayed, seven stars shone at Hoshimiya Shrine, so the village came to be called Hoshizaki.* Owarishi says, ``The place name of Koreru Hoshizaki is based on the Seisha Shrine, and even though it seems like the first hundred poems of the poem called Hoshizaki, in that period it was mostly Oshiha Karururuya,'' and says that Seishi Shrine is the origin of the place name. The Aichi County Magazine also makes the following observation: ``Couldn't the place name Hoshizaki come about because it was owned by Hoshimiya Company?''

* {{ill|Mainichi Shimbun|Q1136866|qid=Q1136866}}'s ``Town name origin record'' (1954) states that the place names Hoshizaki and Narumi arose from the fact that the morning star fell on the inlet on May 24, 1205, {{ill|Genkyū|Q1194276|qid=Q1194276}}<ref name="Minamino Meteorite" />. This tradition is based on Jizo Engi at Shugen Jizo-in Temple, and is also mentioned in the section on Yamazaki Village in the Owari Makiyuki. On the same day, the heavens and earth suddenly trembled, the sea rumbled, and many stars shone like thunder. However, when the villagers went out to sea, there were no traces left. From this time, ``Narumi'' began to be written as ``Narumi,'' and the place where the morning star descended began to be called ``Hoshizaki.''As for reliable records, {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}}9 {{jalink|August 14th} (Lunar calendar)|Q840163|August 14th}} ({{ill|1632|Q6865|qid=Q6865}}{{ill|September 27|Q2884|qid=Q2884}}), there is a "Minamino meteorite" that fell in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Minamino Village}}, which was a village next to Honchi Village. The situation at that time is depicted in the appendix ``Ojida no Shimizu'' of the Owari Meisho Zue. The meteorite was stored in a private house as a ``star stone'', but in 12 years ({{ill|1829|Q7572|qid=Q7572}}), it was donated to Yobitsugisha Shrine in the same village, and became its {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}. The wooden box containing the meteorite has the words ``spirit stone'' written on the front. On August 15, 1976, Sadao Murayama of {{ill|National Museum of Nature and Science|Q74940|qid=Q74940}} identified it as a meteorite and named it the "Minamino Meteorite." Currently, it is the second oldest meteorite in Japan, after the {{ill|Nōgata meteorite|Q1995438|qid=Q1995438}}, for which the age of the meteorite is known.

There is a legend that a meteorite fell in this area in the 8th and 13th centuries. Part of it is thought to refer to the above-mentioned traditions from the 5th year of Johei (935) and the 2nd year of Genkyu (1205). Please note that Seimiya Shrine is not the site of a meteorite fall or that it is enshrined as a divine object.

=== Tradition about Taira no Masakado's prayer ===
At Kasadera, there are some ruins related to the tradition of the prayer for Taira no Masakado's chofu, which is mentioned in the Owari Makigyoki.

* Kagutsuchi Shrine (Akiba Shrine), located to the west of Kasadera Elementary School, is the place where the mikoshi of Atsuta Shrine was passed over, and has the old name of Mikoshiyama (Mikoshiyama).

* Kasadera Shichisho Shrine <ref name="Shichisho Shrine" /> is said to have been a place where the Seven Gods of Atsuta were summoned to pray for the peace of the world, as there was a spiritual experience in the prayer of Taira no Masakado at Seimiya Shrine.

* At Mt. Tanpachi, north of Kasadera Elementary School, there is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Taira no Masakado's head mound}}. Tanpachizan is not a historical site, but a park maintained and donated by {{ill|Tanpachiro Ishikawa|Q28122554|qid=Q28122554}}, but the company's editorial confirms that it is a sacred place for Kasadera Shichisho Shrine.

There is also a legend that ``seven pillars'' {{ill|Sea mark|Q98272210|qid=Q98272210|lt=marker}} were erected for ships traveling to and from Otsu, southwest of Honchi Village. In addition to the ``seven stars'' that appear in the legend of Taira no Masakado Chofu, numbers such as seven faces, seven pillars, and seven star crests suggest that Seishimiya Shrine was recognized from an early stage as a shrine based on the Myoken faith.

=== Precinct Company ===
The Kanbun Memorandum (Memorandum of Kanbun Villages) states that there is one guardian deity, ``Hoshimiya, Tennozan, and two shrines.''

The Owari Makiyuki records that there are five shrines: Setsusha Sochi Gama Shrine, Shimo Chi Gama Shrine, Shinmei Tenno Soden, Inari Akiba Soden, and Reisha.

The Owarishi records that there are seven shrines: Kamichigamasya, Shimochigamasya, Shinmeisha Tennosoden, Reisha, Inarisha Akibasoden, Akibasha, and Konpirasha.

In the illustration of ``Hoshi no Miya'' in {{ill|Owari meisho zue|ff|Owari meisho zue|ja|尾張名所図会|qid=Q11465290}}, from the left side by head office, ``Konpira, Shinmei, Head Office, Inari, Akiha, Rei-sha'' are annotated, and the two u on the hill behind them are annotated with ``Inatsuwokinano-sha''.

There are currently nine shrines in the precincts, as listed below.
*Setsusha Kamichigama Shrine
* Setsusha Shimochigama Shrine
* Hakusansha
* Kotohirasha
* Tennosha Shinmeisha Hall
* Kagudosha
* Kyutsuchisha
* Shrine
* Heroisha

=== Festival ===
* Regular festival: First Sunday of October and the day before (Honji festival)

=== About Shimochigama Shrine ===
[[Image:Kamichikama-sha Shrine & Shimochikama-sha Shrine, Miyanishi Motohoshizaki-cho Minami Ward Nagoya 2021.jpg|thumb|Kamichigama Shrine (image right) / Shimochigama Shrine (image left) (August 2021)]]

=== Enshrined God ===

==== Nodomeyo (Kamichigamama Shrine) ====
Mashiki Toju no Mikoto, Ina Tochi Old Man (Shimochigama Shrine).

On the mountaintop behind the main shrine, there are two shrines, Kamichigama Shrine and Shimochigama Shrine, which enshrine the two parent deities {{ill|Takeinadane|Q11486691|qid=Q11486691}} and {{ill|Miyazu-hime|Q11455216|qid=Q11455216|lt=Miyazanohime-no-Mikoto}}. The two pillars, as {{ill|Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11465294|qid=Q11465294}}, set up a castle in Hidaka (present-day Otaka, the site of {{ill|Hikami Anego Shrine|Q11549548|qid=Q11549548}}) in the southeast, and their descendants {{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311}} served as the Daiguji family of Atsuta Shrine.

Owarishi and Owari enshrine the two deities enshrined at the Shimosha as Mashiki Katana no Mikoto and Ina Tochiroo. The Owari Makiyuki records that there is a small shrine dedicated to ``Ina Tochio'' at the peak of Hoshimiya Shrine. The Owari Meisho Zue depicts ``Inatsuwokinano-sha'' on the top of the mountain behind the main shrine. According to the explanation in Minami Ward, Chigama Shrine enshrines the old man Inatsuchi, but it does not explicitly say whether it is one of the upper or lower shrines.According to the Minami Ward commentary, Old Man Ina Tochi is the person who introduced {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=salt production}} to the area. Owari Makiyuki records that he was the first person to bring the technique of baking solid salt in a clay oven to this area, and that he was the ``ancestor god of clay ovens'' that was enshrined to reward his efforts. Owarishi says that the old man Ina Tochi is a divine name that honors the person who brought the technique of burning sea salt using Shiogama to this area. According to the {{ill|Kiki (Shinto)|ja|記紀|ko|기키|pl|Kiki (literatura japońska)|zh|記紀|qid=Q842308}}, the name should have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiotsuchiroo}}, but the name Ina Tochiroo is used as proof that he inherited the divine name from before the Middle Ages. This area used to be the coastline, and salt production was popular.

=== Shikinai Chigama Shrine ===
Kamichigama Shrine and Shimochigama Shrine are small shrines (shikinai shrines) listed in Aichi District, Owari Province in the Engishiki Shikimyocho. Chigama-jinja Shrine in Hoshimiya-sha Setsusha, along with Chigama-jinja Shrine in Atsuta-jingu Setsusha, is a non-sha of Chigama-jinja Shrine within this ceremony. There is an opinion that Hoshimiya Shrine's Chigama Shrine is the former shrine of Atsuta Shrine's Chigama Shrine.

Although Owarishi declined, saying, ``I continue to write exhaustively with some speculation,'' he added the following considerations.

* The reason why the portable shrine of Atsuta Shrine was handed over to Seishimiya Shrine for the prayer for Taira no Masakado's shofu is that the two shrines had a deep relationship from that time, similar to that of the shrine outside the shrine and the main shrine. In later generations, the reason why Shimochigama Shrine was moved to the market town of Atsuta Shrine (then Gendayu Shrine, now Kamichigama Shrine, Atsuta Shrine Precincts Setsusha) and Hatayacho (at that time Kitayu Shrine, now Shimochigama Shrine, Atsuta Shrine Precincts Setsusha) is said to be because of their deep relationship.

* ``Aichi-gun Chiba-go'' in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wamyo Ruijusho}} is the old place name of Hoshizaki Seven Villages, and it is incorrect to call Atsuta Chiba-sho in early modern times. It is said that the reason why Shimochigama Shrine in Atsuta was called Gendayu-sha and Kitayu-sha until early modern times is because it was not ``Chigama'' (Chigata). Furthermore, the fact that the lower shrine is located closer to the main shrine, contrary to the hierarchy of the two shrines, is evidence that the shrine was moved from another location. Furthermore, {{ill|Dai Nippon Chimei Jisho|Q17213149|qid=Q17213149}} compares Hoshizaki to Sakura-go rather than Senbaku-go, despite the quotation from Owarishi.

* It is said that in ancient times, the Shimochigama Shrine was enshrined in two separate locations, the upper and lower, of the Hoshizaki Seven Villages in Chiba-go.{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092}} says about Shimochigama Shrine, ``Shimochigama Shrine was also located in a place called Shimochigo in Kamiko, and later moved here. He wrote, "My mother-in-law said, ``My mother-in-law should be prayed for, and I have prepared for my thoughts.''" and, similar to Owarishi, it is said that the names of upper and lower are the names of places in the Motomiya of Chiba-go.

=== Related shrines ===

=== Kegutsuchisha ===
Address: 726 Terasaka, Honhoshizaki-cho, Minami-ku, Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture

Enshrined deity: (unknown)

Former Mukakusha. Also called Akibasha. The main enshrined deity is thought to be {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|Q1640658|qid=Q1640658|lt=Kigutsuchi no Mikoto}}.

It is enshrined on Mikoshiyama to the west of Kasadera Elementary School, where prayers for Taira no Masakado's death were held. Mikoshiyama is also referred to as ``Mikoshizuka'' and ``Shichimenzuka'' in the Owari Makiyuki. It is said that {{ill|Life release|Q11078912|qid=Q11078912}} has been held here to tell the story of the past.

There is no mention in the Owari Makiyuki that there is a shrine on that mountain. The company name is mentioned in the Aichi County Magazine published in the Taisho era.

=== Kanjosha ===
Address: 146 Hoshizaki 1-chome, Minami-ku, Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture

Deities enshrined: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu no Okami}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kunijotachison}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Keirigison}}

Old village company. It is also referred to as ``Shinmei Shrine'' in the Owari Makiyuki and ``Yotsugu Shinmeisha'' in the Owari Chronicles.

The Minamino meteorite is considered a sacred object.

=== Shichisho Shrine ===
Address: 1-24 Kasutake-cho, Minami-ku, Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture

Deities enshrined: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nippon Takeru}}, {{ill|Miyazu-hime|Q11455216|qid=Q11455216|lt=Miyazakihime no Mikoto}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Uga Mitama no Mikoto}}, { {jalink|Nostopyo-mikoto|Q97706258}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Susa-no-o-mikoto}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amanohinomi-mikoto}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaninho-no-mikoto}}

Old town company. It is also referred to as ``Shichisho Myo Shrine'' and ``Shichisho Shrine'' in the Owari Makiyuki.

It is said that during the {{ill|Tengyō|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340}} years (938 - 947), the prayer for the Taira no Masakado chofu held at Hoshizaki had divine power, so he solicited the Atsuta Seven Shrines to pray for the peace of the nation. {{ill|Fuken Gōsha Meiji Jinja Shiryō|Q11486103|qid=Q11486103|lt=Meiji Shrine Journal Materials}} notes that the year of its founding was {{ill|Eishō (Heian period)|Q1193549|qid=Q1193549}} years (1046 - 1053) and that it ``looks like a book.'' The Aichi County Magazine says, ``According to the shrine biography, it was a solicitation during the Eisho era.''
